_description: Astronomical reference data — external values from IAU, JPL, Meeus, Souami & Souchay. Nothing model-specific. Source of truth for both tools/lib/constants/astro-reference.js and src/script.js.

nutationLeadingTermsArcsec._description: IAU 1980 nutation, four leading terms. dPsi (longitude) = psiOmega*sin(Om) + psi2Ls*sin(2Ls) + psi2Lm*sin(2Lm) + psi2Omega*sin(2Om); dEps (obliquity) = epsOmega*cos(Om) + eps2Ls*cos(2Ls) + eps2Lm*cos(2Lm) + eps2Omega*cos(2Om). Om = lunar ascending node longitude (the model's own nodal machinery is the driver), Ls/Lm = mean solar/lunar longitudes. Units arcsec.

physicalConstants._massRatioNote: SYSTEM = planet + its moons; ALONE = planet only. They differ materially where a massive satellite exists — Pluto/Charon by 10.85%. Mercury and Venus have no moons, so ALONE = SYSTEM and src/script.js derives it rather than storing a second copy; Earth-alone is likewise derived via MASS_RATIO_EARTH_MOON.

smallBodyMasses._description: Ceres from Dawn radiometric tracking (2015-2018). Eros measured by NEAR Shoemaker (2000-2001). Halley's is an ESTIMATE from size (~11x8x8 km) and density (~0.6 g/cm3) — no spacecraft has orbited it.

physicalConstants._parallaxChainNote: Two more members of the appendix parallax chain (see _earthRadiiNote): solarParallaxArcsec is the IAU 1976 defining constant; arcsecDisplacementKm is the 1-arcsec displacement at 1 AU, the historical-chain primitive the website builds its ONE_AU_KM from (displacement x 648000/pi = 149,597,870.6988278 — matches currentAUDistance to 0.2 mm at stored precision; the radius/parallax route reproduces AU to ~8 m, the documented tiny inconsistency). Consumed by the model-values registry (solarParallax / arcsecDisplacement keys); the browser uses neither directly.
physicalConstants._earthRadiiNote: TWO radius quantities, deliberately distinct. earthEquatorialRadiusKm = IAU 2015 nominal equatorial radius (geodetic convention; the correct radius for the J2 figure-of-Earth term). earthParallaxRadiusKm = the parallax-consistent radius, matched pair of currentAUDistance via the appendix chain: r / solarParallax(8.794143836 arcsec) x (648000/pi) = 149,597,870.698828 km. The website's EARTH_RADIUS_KM and the earthRadius/Diameter/Circumference display keys use the parallax radius. Merging them would conflate a geodetic convention with the parallax/AU system's length (IAU 1976 a_E was 6378.140) — same unit-conflation class as LOD-days vs SI-days.

earthOrbital._obliquityJ2000Note: IAU 2006 (84381.406 arcsec / 3600, Capitaine et al. 2003) — adopted at the 12e refit (full Step 0 + 6a-6e + corrections regeneration under this anchor; the prior IAU 1976/1980 deferral note is in git history).

bodyDiametersKm._description: Mean body diameters in km. NOT presentation-only: earthDiameter yields R_EARTH_M for the physics, and sunDiameter/moonDiameter give the radii the eclipse geometry uses. Halley's and Eros are irregular; the figure is a mean.

cardinalPointAnchors._comment: The observed 2000 cardinal instants, UTC — USNO Astronomical Applications Department, 'Earth's Seasons: Equinoxes, Solstices, Perihelion, and Aphelion' (minute precision: VE Mar 20 07:35, SS Jun 21 01:48, AE Sep 22 17:27, WS Dec 21 13:37; SS = juneSolstice2000_JD). Reference data only — no runtime reads them (the cardinal instants are createModel().cardinal, the apparent crossings of the one Sun); the pipeline verifier's informational rows, doc 110 and the model-values registry quote them. Before plan 06 R4d the VE/AE entries were retired-device anchors (05:43 / 19:19 UT), 112 min off these instants.

moonReference._comment: Option C+ (2026-06): sidereal month + apsidal/nodal precession periods are the J2000 anchors. FRAME NOTE: the *ICRF key names are legacy — the VALUES are the EQUINOX-OF-DATE periods (Meeus/IERS observables); the star-referenced periods are the N-/+13 partners (apsidal 3232.60 d, nodal 6793.48 d). Anomalistic and nodal months are derived kinematically. Deep-time evolution: N_apsidal,N_nodal scale as H(t)^2 (T_apsidal*H = const law). I-CONVENTION (v4 E3c): moonEclipticInclinationJ2000 = 5.1573 is the Moon's DYNAMICAL mean osculating inclination (measured from the Meeus series via the h-vector over 2 node cycles) — the physically-correct orbital-plane tilt and D1-lab calibration target; moonInclinationConstantBrownELP = 5.1453964 is the Brown/ELP THEORY CONSTANT (latitude sinF-coefficient normalization: 5.128122/0.99665), kept as the documented partner. Pure gravity maps between the two at 0.01% (lab compression 0.9944).
moonReference._comment_moonObliquity: Measured obliquity of the lunar spin axis to the ecliptic (the only independently MEASURED member of the moonTilt composition). Cassini-state DERIVED to 0.30 percent by direct Euler integration of the full rigid-body rotation (1.5470 deg, tools/explore/moon-euler-rotation.js) from GRAIL/LLR J2/C22/C-MR2 + framework rates; the fixed-axis averaged balance gives 1.5551 deg and the libration-pole coupling it cannot contain accounts for 64 percent of that gap - tools/explore/cassini-moontilt.js, docs/66 par 1. The scene mesh tilt composes moonEclipticInclinationJ2000 + this value so the rendered spin-to-ecliptic obliquity equals the measured 1.5424.
moonReference._comment_moonTilt: Catalog CONVENTION-COMPOSED axial tilt: Brown/ELP constant 5.1453964 + measured obliquity 1.5424 = 6.6878. Kept for display/reference; the scene geometry uses the composition in its own (dynamical-inclination) convention.

moonMeeus._description: Lunar mean longitude coefficients (Meeus Ch. 47). Full perturbation tables in tools/lib/constants/meeus-lunar-tables.json.

elpW1T2Decomposition_arcsecPerCy2._comment: Chapront, Chapront-Touze & Francou (2002, A&A 387, 700): W1 T^2 parts on the inertial ecliptic J2000. Frame bridge to Meeus's of-date L': add p_A T^2 (Lieske 1976 for the Meeus-era polynomial; IAU2006 modern). Attributes the framework's Lp planetary T^2 remainder with zero free parameters: remainder +7.247 = planetary + earthFigureJ2 + p_A(Lieske) + 0.077 Meeus-era tidal-convention gap (Gamma embedded -25.706 vs LLR -25.858). See tools/explore/v4-kpl-budget.js.

planetOrbitalElements._description: JPL/SPICE J2000 orbital elements per planet

additionalBodiesReference._description: J2000 orbital elements for the four additional bodies, mirroring planetOrbitalElements. Previously only 2-3 fields per body lived here and the rest were literals in src/script.js with no source of truth.

moonGrailWilliams2014._description: Lunar degree-2 gravity + polar moment citations (GRAIL + LLR; Williams et al. 2014): unnormalized J2 and C22 in units of 1e-6, and C/MR2. Inputs of the Cassini-state moontilt labs (tools/explore/cassini-moontilt.js, moon-euler-rotation.js — which carry local copies) and the model-values registry (moonJ2Grail / moonC22Grail / moonCMR2 keys). Citations, never model inputs.

giaCoxChaoPeltier._description: GIA calibration literature anchors: Cox & Chao (2002, Science 297) satellite-gravimetry dJ2/dt and the Peltier ICE-6G LOD-coupling axisymmetric-GIA J2-to-alpha conversion factor. The SHIPPED product is the calibrated alphaClimateScalePerMille (model-parameters deepTime — calibrated so dalpha/dt at J2000 = dJ2Dt/factor = -1.35e-11/yr); these two are the citation inputs of that calibration, consumed only by the model-values registry (coxChaoDJ2Dt / giaJ2ToAlphaFactor / derived dAlphaDtJ2000 keys). The browser carries them in comments only (script.js ~:2375).

obliquityChapront2002._description: Chapront, Chapront-Touze & Francou (2002, A&A 387, 700) obliquity citation values at the ±12 kyr comparison epochs. Consumed by the model-values registry (obliqChapront* keys) for the Model-vs-literature obliquity tables; the website previously typed these as literals.

planetSpinObserved._description: Observed planetary spin-precession constants and J2000 obliquities — CITATION values for the Stage-C-4 spin/Cassini landscape (doc 109 §19; the labs tools/explore/stage-c4-*.mjs and the spinLandscape* registry keys). Comparison targets ONLY, never model inputs. Sources: Mars spin precession −7608.3 ± 2.1 mas/yr (Konopliv et al. 2016, Icarus 274, 253; InSight combined −7605 ± 3, Kahan et al. 2021, PSS 199) quoted at −7.606 ″/yr; Jupiter α ≈ −2.7…−2.9 ″/yr moment-of-inertia-dependent (Saillenfest, Lari & Courtot 2020, A&A 640, A11), quoted midrange −2.8; Saturn present pole rate ≈ −0.45 ″/yr = ~68% of the long-term rate via the 700-yr Titan cycle, captured in the s8 resonance (Ward & Hamilton 2004, AJ 128, 2501); Mercury Cassini-state lock confirmed by Margot et al. (2007, Science 316, 710). Obliquities (IAU/Archinal et al. WGCCRE): Mars 25.19°, Jupiter 3.13°, Saturn 26.73°.

planetSpinPhysical._description: The planets' spin-channel INPUTS (plan 06 Phase 7, ex-K8b-3): each planet's degree-2 gravity, polar moment of inertia, IAU spin pole and rotation rate, and its regular satellites — the torque side of the precession constant α = (3/2)(n²/ω)(1−e²)^(−3/2)·(J₂+q)/(λ+l) (Ward & Hamilton 2004, AJ 128, 2501, eqs. 1–3: q = ½Σ(m_i/M)(a_i/R)², l = Σ(m_i/M)(a_i/R)²(n_i/ω)); the orbital side (a, e, mean motion, the orbit-plane history n̂(t)) is the model's own N-body chain and its deep ζ tables. ONE HOME: packages/physics/src/planets/spin-channel.cjs. MATCHED PAIRS: j2 is quoted at its source's reference radius j2ReferenceRadiusKm (J₂R² is the physical quantity; a_i/R uses the same radius). momentOfInertiaFactorClass names how λ = C/MR² was obtained — 'spin-inferred' (from the measured precession rate, so the channel's rate for that planet is a CLOSURE of the source, not an independent test), 'gravity-constrained' (interior models fitted to the measured J₂–J₆, independent of the spin), 'interior-model' (no measurement; a modelled class). rotationRateDegPerDay is the IAU W-dot, SIGNED (negative = retrograde rotation: Venus, Uranus); the channel spins on the angular-momentum direction = the IAU north pole times the sign. Satellite GM values are the ephemeris masses; only the regular satellites that matter for q enter (Mars's two are kept for completeness; retrograde Triton carries its sign in l). POLES are the J2000 spin direction the integration starts from, so they are the IAU expressions EVALUATED at J2000, not their constant terms: the 2015 Mars model writes the pole as a precession-cone centre (317.269202°, 54.432516°) plus a 1.59° circle term, which at J2000 evaluates to (317.681°, 52.887°) = the 2009 constants used here (NASA Mars fact sheet: 317.681, 52.887; obliquity to orbit 25.19°); Neptune's constant terms (299.36°, 43.46°) are the MEAN pole about which the 688-yr Triton-forced nutation (0.70° sin N, 0.51° cos N) turns — the channel integrates the secular precession only, so it starts from the mean pole and its J2000 obliquity (27.85°) is the mean-pole value, 0.5° below the instantaneous IAU tilt 28.32°. SOURCES — pole/rotation: IAU WGCCRE 2015 report (Archinal et al. 2018, CMDA 130, 22) as carried by NAIF pck00011.tpc; satellites: JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters (GM, ephemerides MAR097/JUP365/SAT441/URA111/NEP097) and Planetary Satellite Orbital Parameters (mean a, P); Mercury J₂ 5.03e-5 (Smith et al. 2012, Science 336, 214) and C/MR² 0.346 ± 0.014 (Margot et al. 2012, JGR 117, E00L09); Venus J₂ 4.4044e-6 at 6051 km (MGNP180U, Konopliv et al. 1999, Icarus 139, 3) and C/MR² 0.337 ± 0.024 inferred from the measured pole precession 44.58 ± 3.3 ″/yr (Margot et al. 2021, Nat. Astron. 5, 676); Mars J₂ 1.956608e-3 at 3396 km and C/MR² 0.3644 ± 0.0005 inferred from ψ̇ = −7608.3 ± 2.1 mas/yr (MRO120D, Konopliv et al. 2016, Icarus 274, 253); Jupiter J₂ 14696.572e-6 at 71492 km (Juno, Iess et al. 2018, Nature 555, 220) and C/MR² 0.26393 ± 0.00001 from the gravity-constrained CMS models (Militzer & Hubbard 2023, PSJ 4, 95; the empirical two-layer Juno fits of Ni 2018, A&A 613, A32, give 0.2749–0.2762 — kept as the alternative); Saturn J₂ 16290.573e-6 at 60330 km (Cassini Grand Finale, Iess et al. 2019, Science 364, eaat2965) and C/MR² 0.2181 ± 0.0002 (Militzer & Hubbard 2023; the s8-libration inference of Ward & Hamilton 2004 is 0.2257–0.2438 — kept as the alternative band); Uranus J₂ 3510.68e-6 at 25559 km (Jacobson 2014, AJ 148, 76) and Neptune J₂ 3408.43e-6 at 25225 km (Jacobson 2009, AJ 137, 4322), their C/MR² the interior-model class (Helled et al. 2011, ApJ 726, 15). Mercury is Cassini-locked (Margot et al. 2007, Science 316, 710): its spin follows the orbit node; the channel reports α_free/|s| as the lock statement and the shipped axial row stays the chain's node rate.

ascendingNodesSouamiSouchay._description: Raw ascending nodes on invariable plane from Souami & Souchay (2012) Table 2. invariablePlaneOnEclipticDeg is the PLANE's own ascending node on the ecliptic (107°34'56" — docs/05), consumed only by the model-values registry.

laplaceLagrangeBounds._description: Inclination bounds from Farside Table 10.4 (Brouwer & van Woerkom). Units: degrees.

jplEclipticInclinationTrends._description: JPL ecliptic inclination trend rates (degrees/century). Source: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html

eigenmodePhasesLaplaceLagrange._description: Laplace-Lagrange inclination eigenmode phase angles (degrees). Source: Farside Table 10.1.

externalCurveAnchors._description: Offsets used ONLY to re-anchor a published external curve onto the model's axis for comparison. Never inputs — nothing downstream of the model reads them.

knownValues._description: Validation reference values for comparison (used by moon-cycles.js and the model-values registry). Moon month inputs are in moonReference — not duplicated here. The meeus*/sunModel* entries are the docs/66 validation-campaign statistics (Meeus-vs-JPL and Sun-model residuals) — recorded snapshots, same maintenance class as the campaign summary JSONs in data/. meeusA1RateDegPerCy duplicates the A1 rate embedded in the script.js Meeus series (:26562), recorded here so the registry derives rather than types it. moonKeplerEffectiveDistanceKm is the DLT-1 section-3 three-body semi-major axis (vs two-body Kepler 384,748 km — docs/66 'which a'). llrTidalGammaArcsecPerCy2 is the LLR tidal acceleration (the alpha-1 chain anchor).
knownValues._frameworkAccuracyNote: E4/E5 + 20.3h campaign accuracy measurements (registry keys frameworkSun*/moonSeries*): the certified framework-native Sun's apparent-longitude RMS vs JPL over the modern window, the Meeus Ch. 25 reference measured on the same window and instrument, and the shipped derived lunar series' all-phase lambda/beta RMS vs JPL after the round-2 Delaunay tail (docs 66 and 99).
knownValues._mainstreamNote: mainstream* entries: conventional-theory literature values for the Model-vs-mainstream precession/obliquity comparison tables (registry mainstream* keys) — rounded kyr labels and the exact-comparison variants.
knownValues._perihelionRatesNote: Perihelion-rate comparison values (registry keys): mercuryNewtonian/ObservedICRF/AnomalyClassic are the textbook chain (532 + 43 = 575 arcsec/cy); Park 2017 is the MESSENGER-era determination; the *ObservedRateArcsecCy entries are WebGeocalc 1900-2000 trend readings (earth geocentric wrt moving equinox AND heliocentric ICRF; venus ~0 flips sign across sub-windows; saturn ecliptic-retrograde, with its missing-advance bridge to geocentric). ascNodeJointRmsArcsec is the joint RA/Dec RMS of the ascending-node correction fit run (the fitter tools/fit/ascnode-correction.js prints it; a --write mode is future work, same class as the campaign generators).
knownValues._classicalSystemNote: The classical (Le Verrier→Newcomb→Clemence) reduction system for Mercury's perihelion, in ecliptic longitude of date: generalPrecessionNewcomb is Newcomb's general precession used in those reductions; mercuryObservedLonOfDateClemence is Clemence 1947 (Rev. Mod. Phys. 19, 361) — the 1765–1937 longitudes vs the equinox of date, 5599.74 ± 0.41; mercuryNewtonianClassical is his Newtonian subtotal 5557.18 minus Newcomb's precession. Doc 13 §1.8, tools/explore/mercury-perihelion-frames.mjs.
knownValues._deepTimeAnchorsNote: Deep-time literature/derived anchors for the registry epoch tables: Patterson 1956 Pb-Pb Earth age; the moon-genesis age (rigid-Roche crossing of the Farhat recession polynomial — derived once, doc 102 chain); Wells 1963 coral tidal rate and its recession equivalent; the modern LLR recession (Dickey 1994 / Chapront 2002 — the framework's alpha-1 anchor); the tidal-lock approach horizon and the ESSRT formula horizon (prose estimates).
knownValues._climateNullTestNote: Doc 97/98/103 campaign snapshots for the registry: the long-band ice-albedo share (doc 97 table — the per-regime artifact carries only the three sub-130-kyr bands), the Cheng 2016 cross-proxy R2, the Test A action-angle closure results, the LA2004 8H-commensurability percentile, and the Test C series (doc 97 section 4.9). Generators are the docs/97-98 analysis scripts; same maintenance class as the other campaign snapshots.
knownValues._meeusPeriLongNote: Meeus (1998) Earth perihelion-longitude citation values at the comparison epochs (registry periLongMeeus* keys).

galaxyMotion._description: Sun and galaxy motion parameters (visualization only)

timeReference._description: Calendar and epoch reference values (IAU / standard definitions). j2000JD is JD of J2000.0 (2000 Jan 1.5 TT); julianCenturyDays is the IAU Julian century (365.25 x 100 days); gregorianStartJD is the start of the Gregorian calendar (1582 Oct 15); jd1800/jd1900/jd2100 are ~Jan 1 calendar reference points used by display ranges.

perihelionPrecessionRatesJPL._description: Observed perihelion precession rates in arcsec/century, 1900-2100 trend. Source: JPL SPICE/WebGeoCalc. These fluctuate over time and are not valid for long-term predictions. Validation reference only, never a model input. Saturn is retrograde over this window.

juneSolsticeReference._description: Reference June solstice Julian Dates (source: astropixels.com, Jean Meeus algorithms). JD convention: JD X.5 = midnight UTC, JD X.0 = noon UTC. Leaf is named solsticeRefJD (not jd, not solsticeJD) because tools/constants/check-literals.mjs name-matches leaf keys and both shorter names occur as numeric declarations in script.js. Validation reference only.
